prompt_text: Where should I buy tires in Pleasanton CA and who does the best installation?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: go where you can buy the tires you want at a good price and have them mounted by a shop with strong local reviews that offers proper mounting/balancing, TPMS service, and a clear warranty/road‑hazard policy.

Which places to consider
- Big warehouse / membership stores: Costco Tire Center — often competitive prices and good road‑hazard coverage, but you must be a member and appointments can book up.
- Large specialty chains: Discount Tire, Firestone Complete Auto Care, Pep Boys, Big O — convenient, nationwide warranty options and usually same‑day installs.
- Local independent tire shops / tire centers — can offer very competitive pricing, faster appointments, and personal service; quality varies by shop.
- Dealership service departments — typically pricier, but technicians know model‑specific torque/TPMS/installation procedures.

How to pick the best installer (quick checklist to use when calling or reading reviews)
- Read recent Google/Yelp reviews for “tire installation” and “mount/balance” quality.
- Confirm the shop will: install new valve stems, mount and balance, torque lug nuts to manufacturer spec, reset TPMS if needed.
- Ask about included services: road‑hazard/warranty coverage, free rotation/alignment, disposal fees.
- Ask whether they use computerized balancing and whether they guarantee ride vibration resolution (re‑balance if vibration persists).
- Check certifications (ASE, manufacturer dealer for certain brands) and how long they’ve been in business.
- Compare total out‑the‑door price: tires + mount/balance + taxes + shop fees + alignment (alignment is often recommended after new tires).
- Ask about appointment availability and lead time.

Practical tips for the install
- Get an alignment after installing new tires unless the shop confirms alignment is within spec.
- Keep receipts and any warranty/road‑hazard paperwork.
- Confirm they torque wheel lug nuts to the vehicle manufacturer specification and recommend re‑torque after 50–100 miles.

If you want, I can:
- Recommend specific tire models based on your vehicle and driving (commute, highway, performance, light truck, winter needs).
- Look up and list highly rated tire shops and addresses in Pleasanton if you give me your ZIP or allow me to search now.

Which would you prefer—specific local shop recommendations, or tire model recommendations (vehicle + driving style)?
